wild_hist_scarlatti_needle_harpsichord.name: wild_hist_scarlatti_needle_harpsichord
wild_hist_scarlatti_needle_harpsichord.description: Domenico Scarlatti / Venetian-Madrid harpsichord sonata copyist: razor-thin needle-slash noteheads, crow-quill hairlines, and crisp forward velocity.
wild_hist_scarlatti_needle_harpsichord.paleography_notes: Inspired by mid-18th-century Venice/Parma/Madrid harpsichord sonata manuscripts (Scarlatti circle, c. 1742-1757): sharply pared crow-quill producing hairline stems and ultra-slim needle-slash noteheads (aspect 0.30, scale 0.68), rapid right-leaning ductus, crisp sharp-V and Baroque C-hook rests, and clear iron-gall brown ink on smooth cream Italian laid paper.

wild_hist_couperin_pinprick_clavecin.name: wild_hist_couperin_pinprick_clavecin
wild_hist_couperin_pinprick_clavecin.description: Versailles clavecin ornament manuscript (Couperin circle): tiny pinprick noteheads, gossamer crow-quill stems, and lavishly scrolled French clefs.
wild_hist_couperin_pinprick_clavecin.paleography_notes: Models Parisian and Versailles clavecin manuscripts (c. 1713-1730): miniature pinprick-dot noteheads (scale 0.54, aspect 0.48) leaving generous room for dense agréments, gossamer crow-quill lines (stroke_scale 0.52), elaborate French violin/soprano clefs (clef_ornate 0.98), and calligraphic S-curl and Baroque flag-loop rests.

wild_hist_frescobaldi_lozenge_choirbook.name: wild_hist_frescobaldi_lozenge_choirbook
wild_hist_frescobaldi_lozenge_choirbook.description: Early-Baroque Roman choirbook & toccata hand (c. 1624): broad-nib lozenge noteheads, chiseled thick-thin contrast, and dark walnut iron-gall on heavy rag.
wild_hist_frescobaldi_lozenge_choirbook.paleography_notes: Models early-17th-century Roman keyboard and polyphonic choirbook scribes (Frescobaldi / St. Peter's Cappella Giulia, c. 1615-1635): wide chisel-cut goose quill (48 deg, 0.16 min-ratio) forming bold broad-nib lozenge noteheads (scale 1.24, aspect 1.15), upright ceremonial ductus, heavy iron-gall pooling, and mottled thick rag folio paper.

wild_hist_monteverdi_mantua_diamond.name: wild_hist_monteverdi_mantua_diamond
wild_hist_monteverdi_mantua_diamond.description: Early-Baroque Mantuan/Venetian dramatic manuscript (c. 1610): narrow slim-diamond mensural heads, corroded iron-gall bleed, and wavy hand-drawn rastrum staves.
wild_hist_monteverdi_mantua_diamond.paleography_notes: Evokes Mantuan and Venetian early-17th-century theatrical manuscripts (c. 1607-1620): transitional slim-diamond noteheads (aspect 0.44) written rapidly with a sharp broad-edge quill, pronounced iron-gall acid feathering and ghost bleed-through, wavy 5-nib rastrum staves, and archaic flag-loop and C-hook rests.

wild_hist_vivaldi_pieta_hairline_dash.name: wild_hist_vivaldi_pieta_hairline_dash
wild_hist_vivaldi_pieta_hairline_dash.description: Furious Venetian concerto draft (Vivaldi / Pietà shorthand): ultra-thin hairline-dash noteheads, dry-brush split-nib skips, and steep flying slant.
wild_hist_vivaldi_pieta_hairline_dash.paleography_notes: Pushes Antonio Vivaldi's fastest Turin working-score shorthand to its calligraphic extreme: noteheads reduced to razor-slim hairline dashes (aspect 0.27, fill_density 0.45), near-maximal forward slant (17.8 deg), heavy dry-quill ink dropout and split-nib tracks, frantic slash-zig and sharp-V rests, and cramped measure endings.

wild_hist_venetian_opera_buffa_slash.name: wild_hist_venetian_opera_buffa_slash
wild_hist_venetian_opera_buffa_slash.description: Frantic Venetian opera-house copyist (Teatro San Moisè, c. 1760): slashing needle noteheads, huge barline overshoots, and candle-lit pit stains.
wild_hist_venetian_opera_buffa_slash.paleography_notes: Models overnight Venetian opera-house copisti rushing orchestral parts before carnival premieres (c. 1755-1770): aggressive needle-slash heads at -48 deg (aspect 0.34, fill_density 0.52), wild barline overshoots (0.85 sp), hurried scribble-S and slash-zig rests, and heavily spotted theater rag paper.

wild_hist_late_bach_tremor_art_of_fugue.name: wild_hist_late_bach_tremor_art_of_fugue
wild_hist_late_bach_tremor_art_of_fugue.description: Late-Bach failing-eyesight contrapuntal score (1749-1750): heavy blotted iron-gall heads, pronounced hand tremor, acid feathering, and deep bleed-through.
wild_hist_late_bach_tremor_art_of_fugue.paleography_notes: Models J.S. Bach's final Leipzig manuscripts (1749-1750, Art of Fugue / B-minor Mass late revisions) when deteriorating vision and hand tremor produced heavy, over-inked blotted noteheads (ink_blot, fill_density 1.42), strong tremor (2.85 px) and wobble (2.90 px), dense iron-gall pooling/feathering, and corrosive bleed-through.

wild_hist_purcell_westminster_rough_quil.name: wild_hist_purcell_westminster_rough_quill
wild_hist_purcell_westminster_rough_quil.description: Restoration English rough goose-quill score (Purcell / Westminster, c. 1685): angular chevron-wedge noteheads, split-nib scratches, and undulating staves.
wild_hist_purcell_westminster_rough_quil.paleography_notes: Models Henry Purcell's Restoration London autographs (British Library Add. MS 30930 / Royal Music Library, c. 1680-1695): sturdy, frequently frayed goose quill (split_nib_prob 0.55) cutting angular chevron-wedge noteheads (aspect 0.72), gritty dry-rag texture, undulating hand-ruled staves, and English Baroque flag-loop and backward-7 rests.

wild_hist_handel_haymarket_boomerang.name: wild_hist_handel_haymarket_boomerang
wild_hist_handel_haymarket_boomerang.description: Handel's impetuous London theater draft (c. 1732): sweeping boomerang-hook noteheads, open half-notes, heavy ink pooling, and slashing barlines.
wild_hist_handel_haymarket_boomerang.paleography_notes: Models G.F. Handel's high-velocity Haymarket Theatre composing drafts: broad wet quill sweeping into hooked boomerang noteheads (aspect 0.50, scale 1.16), frequent unclosed open-loop white notes (hollow_open_prob 0.62), generous barline overshoots (0.78 sp), heavy dark pooling, and abundant marginal singer/tempo cues.

wild_hist_telemann_slim_oval_engraver.name: wild_hist_telemann_slim_oval_engraver
wild_hist_telemann_slim_oval_engraver.description: Hamburg calligraphic fair copy (Telemann circle, c. 1738): poised slim-oval noteheads, whisper-fine steady quill, and immaculate bar geometry.
wild_hist_telemann_slim_oval_engraver.paleography_notes: Models G.P. Telemann's neatest Hamburg print-model fair copies: slender, elongated slim-oval noteheads (aspect 0.42, scale 0.88), finely trimmed steady quill (wobble 0.35 px, stroke_scale 0.74), refined Baroque C-hook and calligraphic S-curl rests, ornate clefs, and razor-even measure proportions on clean cream paper.

wild_hist_pergolesi_naples_open_loop.name: wild_hist_pergolesi_naples_open_loop
wild_hist_pergolesi_naples_open_loop.description: Neapolitan intermezzo autograph (Pergolesi / Conservatorio, c. 1733): airy open-loop noteheads, warm chestnut ink, and fluid Italian cursive.
wild_hist_pergolesi_naples_open_loop.paleography_notes: Models Neapolitan conservatory and San Bartolomeo comic-intermezzo manuscripts (Pergolesi / Vinci / Leo, c. 1730-1736): rapidly looped noteheads left partially hollow/open (open_loop, fill_density 0.42, hollow_open_prob 0.78), warm chestnut iron-gall, graceful 15 deg forward slant, and lively cursive-3 and scribble-S rests.

wild_hist_versailles_philidor_ornamental.name: wild_hist_versailles_philidor_ornamental
wild_hist_versailles_philidor_ornamental.description: Versailles Atelier Philidor royal presentation score (c. 1705): chiseled slim-diamond heads, extreme broad-edge contrast, and maximal calligraphic flourishes.
wild_hist_versailles_philidor_ornamental.paleography_notes: Models André Danican Philidor's royal music workshop at Versailles (c. 1690-1715): crisp chiseled slim-diamond noteheads (aspect 0.52), maximum calligraphic nib contrast (nib_min_ratio 0.15), opulent ornamental clefs (1.0), ceremonial calligraphic S-curl and Baroque flag-loop rests, and regal margins on ivory French rag.

wild_hist_spanish_colonial_cathedral_cuz.name: wild_hist_spanish_colonial_cathedral_cuzco
wild_hist_spanish_colonial_cathedral_cuz.description: Spanish Colonial cathedral villancico & choirbook (Cuzco / Mexico City, c. 1690): giant broad-nib lozenges, rusty-red oxidized iron-gall, and damp-stained rag.
wild_hist_spanish_colonial_cathedral_cuz.paleography_notes: Models late-17th-century Spanish-American cathedral music archives (Cuzco, Puebla, Mexico City, c. 1675-1715): oversized broad-nib lozenge noteheads (scale 1.38, aspect 1.38) cut with a heavy reed or swan quill (stroke_scale 1.82), rust-brown oxidized iron-gall ink, heavy damp-stain mottling, strong bleed-through, and undulating hand-ruled staves.

wild_hist_byrd_tudor_partbook_hollow.name: wild_hist_byrd_tudor_partbook_hollow
wild_hist_byrd_tudor_partbook_hollow.description: Late-Renaissance Tudor consort partbook (Byrd / Gibbons circle, c. 1605): archaic upright hollow-diamond heads, feathered dark umber ink, and coarse rag.
wild_hist_byrd_tudor_partbook_hollow.paleography_notes: Models Elizabethan and Jacobean viol/vocal partbooks (c. 1595-1615, e.g. Dow/Baldwin/My Ladye Nevells Booke scribes): upright, slightly back-leaning hollow-diamond noteheads (aspect 0.62, slant -1.5 deg), absorbent handmade rag causing soft ink feathering (0.48), archaic Baroque flag-loop rests, and pronounced coarse paper grain.

wild_hist_buxtehude_lubeck_vertical_tick.name: wild_hist_buxtehude_lubeck_vertical_tick
wild_hist_buxtehude_lubeck_vertical_tick.description: North German organ-loft shorthand (Lübeck / Buxtehude era, c. 1680): razor-thin vertical-tick noteheads, fine iron-gall nib, and tight contrapuntal bars.
wild_hist_buxtehude_lubeck_vertical_tick.paleography_notes: Models late-17th-century North German organists transferring tablature into dense staff shorthand (Lübeck/Hamburg circle, c. 1675-1700): ultra-narrow vertical-tick noteheads (aspect 0.28, angle -6 deg) drawn with a fine sharp quill (stroke_scale 0.58), upright disciplined ductus, sharp-V and Baroque C-hook rests, and packed contrapuntal measures.

wild_hist_rameau_paris_opera_zigzag.name: wild_hist_rameau_paris_opera_zigzag
wild_hist_rameau_paris_opera_zigzag.description: Paris Opéra turbulent revision draft (Rameau circle, c. 1745): aggressively scribbled zigzag-fill noteheads, pasted-over smudges, and dense rehearsal cues.
wild_hist_rameau_paris_opera_zigzag.paleography_notes: Models Parisian Académie Royale de Musique working scores (Rameau operas, c. 1735-1755) subjected to heavy rehearsal cuts and rewrites: rapidly hatched zigzag-fill noteheads (fill_density 1.35), muscular wobble (2.15 px), frequent scraped/smudged erasures (0.32), scribble-S and hurried slash-zig rests, and crowded marginal stage directions.

wild_hist_cpe_bach_berlin_empfindsam.name: wild_hist_cpe_bach_berlin_empfindsam
wild_hist_cpe_bach_berlin_empfindsam.description: C.P.E. Bach Berlin/Hamburg Empfindsamkeit manuscript (c. 1762): nervous ultra-slim oval noteheads, fine expressive quill, and mercurial rhythmic spacing.
wild_hist_cpe_bach_berlin_empfindsam.paleography_notes: Models Carl Philipp Emanuel Bach's intensely expressive Berlin and Hamburg keyboard autographs (c. 1755-1775): slender, nervous slim-oval noteheads (aspect 0.38, scale 0.78), fine flexible quill (stroke_scale 0.66) with lively forward slant (16.0 deg), mercurial horizontal spacing jitter (0.34), and backward-7 / sharp-V quarter rests.

wild_hist_gluck_vienna_faded_sepia.name: wild_hist_gluck_vienna_faded_sepia
wild_hist_gluck_vienna_faded_sepia.description: Sun-faded Viennese reform-opera folio (Gluck era, c. 1770): pale sepia ink, slim open-loop noteheads, heavy dropout, and ghostly archival bleed-through.
wild_hist_gluck_vienna_faded_sepia.paleography_notes: Models severely sun-faded late-18th-century Viennese court theater archival scores (Gluck / Salieri circle, c. 1765-1780): washed-out pale sepia ink with heavy stroke dropout (0.44), slender open-loop noteheads (aspect 0.46, fill_density 0.36, hollow_open_prob 0.68), strong foxing mottle (0.34), and persistent reverse-side bleed-through.

wild_hist_boccherini_madrid_pinprick_cha.name: wild_hist_boccherini_madrid_pinprick_chamber
wild_hist_boccherini_madrid_pinprick_cha.description: Madrid royal chamber fair copy (Boccherini circle, c. 1778): microscopic pinprick noteheads, needle-fine Spanish crow-quill, and airy elegant phrasing.
wild_hist_boccherini_madrid_pinprick_cha.paleography_notes: Models late-18th-century Madrid court chamber parts (Infante Don Luis / Boccherini quintets, c. 1775-1785): microscopic pinprick-dot noteheads (scale 0.52, aspect 0.65) inked with a razor-fine crow quill (stroke_scale 0.48), minimal wobble (0.40 px), elegant backward-7 and calligraphic S-curl rests, and spacious page geometry.

wild_hist_cimarosa_neapolitan_hairline_r.name: wild_hist_cimarosa_neapolitan_hairline_rush
wild_hist_cimarosa_neapolitan_hairline_r.description: Late-18th-century Neapolitan opera buffa speed-hand (Cimarosa era, c. 1788): extreme 0.25-aspect hairline dashes, maximal slant, and frantic scribble rests.
wild_hist_cimarosa_neapolitan_hairline_r.paleography_notes: Models breakneck late-18th-century Italian comic-opera composing drafts (Cimarosa / Paisiello, c. 1785-1795): noteheads compressed to minimum-aspect hairline dashes (aspect 0.25, fill_density 0.32, scale 0.72), maximum 18 deg forward slant, wild barline overshoots (0.82 sp), dry iron-gall skips, and rapid sharp-V and scribble-S rests.

wild_hist_moravian_colonial_bethlehem_qu.name: wild_hist_moravian_colonial_bethlehem_quill
wild_hist_moravian_colonial_bethlehem_qu.description: Colonial American Moravian Collegium Musicum copyist (Bethlehem, PA, c. 1785): slim chevron-wedge heads, homemade goose quill, and coarse stained colonial rag.
wild_hist_moravian_colonial_bethlehem_qu.paleography_notes: Models Johann Friedrich Peter and Moravian community copyists in Bethlehem and Salem (c. 1770-1795): slim chevron-wedge noteheads (aspect 0.48, scale 0.90) written with hand-cut farmstead goose quills (split_nib_prob 0.34, ink_feather 0.36), warm walnut iron-gall ink on rough locally milled colonial rag paper, and tidy German-tradition backward-7 and C-hook rests.

wild_hist_bohemian_horn_band_blotted_par.name: wild_hist_bohemian_horn_band_blotted_part
wild_hist_bohemian_horn_band_blotted_par.description: Bohemian / Mannheim court Harmoniemusik outdoor partbook (c. 1792): wide blotted ink-blot noteheads, wet feathering, left-leaning stance, and weather stains.
wild_hist_bohemian_horn_band_blotted_par.paleography_notes: Models late-18th-century Bohemian and Mannheim noble wind-band (Harmoniemusik) outdoor performance parts (c. 1785-1795) written bold enough to read by torchlight: wide, heavily inked ink-blot noteheads (aspect 1.65, scale 1.32, fill_density 1.48), heavy wet pooling (0.72) and feathering (0.68), distinctive slight backslant (-6.5 deg), and weather-stained rag paper.
